why:
The other direction of the tie-break (golden-pairs.md section 6 rule 2): when two candidates are identical on EVERY evidence term -- confidence, raw score, identity Alt-ID matches, Alt-ID conflicts -- the order must still be total, so the lower id is proposed, whatever order the candidates arrived in. Before 2026-09-25 the arrival order decided, and BMR-Review measured what that costs: re-running one 731-row batch against the same mirror a day apart changed the proposal between exact-tie duplicates on 5 rows (and the candidate LIST on 327, fixed separately by ordering every capped pool query).

This case: two candidates with identical metadata and no Alt IDs, listed in REVERSE id order. Mutation-tested 2026-09-26: fails under a confidence-only (arrival-order) key; passes under any key that ends in the id, which is the property it pins.

SCOPE: determinism of the proposal among fully tied candidates. Which evidence outranks which is the sibling fixture's job (tie-break-evidence-decides-between-duplicates).

notes: 2 candidates score Accept: likely registry duplicates of each other -- merge review, not a pick
